newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, Arison begin talks on Hapoalim.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Arison begin talks on Hapoalim.

text.p: The Arison group began negotiations this week with the Israeli government on terms for acquiring a controlling stake in Bank Hapoalim Ltd, sources in the Arison group said on Tuesday.

They said the consortium -- one of two competing to buy government shares in Israel's largest commercial bank -- would be offering to buy 34.5 percent of Hapoalim and take an option to acquire another 34.5 percent at an unspecified date.
That would give the group control of nearly all the shares being offered in the tender.
The government holds 78 percent of Hapoalim and the remainder is traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.
The winner of the tender would control the bank even with a minority share holding under terms of the sale.
The sources denied a report in the financial daily Globes published late on Teusday that the group would reconsider its bid if the government did not hold to the timetable for the tender.

They noted that groups competing in the tender have to present their proposals by August 18. Arison group has won all the necessary approvals from the Bank of Israel and the superviser of banks to begin the talks.

The Arison group is 30 percent controlled by Arison Investments, a company controlled by U.S.-Israeli entrepreneur Ted Arison who founded Carnival Cruise Lines. The group includes Claridge Israel, the investment company controlled by Canadian Charles Bronfman; U.S. investor Michael Steinhardt and his partner Shlomo Topor; Israel's Dankner Group; U.S. investment fund Hyperion; and U.S. insurance businessman Len Abramson.
A second group bidding for Hapoalim is led by U.S. banker Jeffrey Keil and Israeli businessman Eliezer Fishman.
The sources said the Arison partners met for three days in New York at the end of last month together with consultants from McKinsey and Co to discuss a valuation for the bank.
Hapoalim shares have risen about 50 percent this year to a market valuation of about $2.6 billion but the shares have fallen in the last week.
A spokesman for Arison said last week the group did not view the market valuation as the value of the bank.
